sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units with finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedule \(Y_i(\cdot)\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps; only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), profile compact order-\(d\) B-spline sieves for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function sieves for \(\phi_1,\phi_2\), and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); use the clipped profiled extrema with deterministic tie-breaking and the stated empty-set rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our contributions include establishing identifiability without any assumption on the noise except for coordinate independence.
We identify the average dose-response function for a continuously valued error contaminated treatment by a weighted conditional expectation.

body.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper: analytic cocycle identification enables an explicit uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band, while a fixed-nuisance marked modulus determines the optimal expected width. At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), the upper procedure combines compact B-spline signal sieves, finite atomic characteristic-function sieves, simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel radii, and the multinomial region for \(p_x\); clipped profiled extrema target width \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\). The lower headline asks for valid Bernoulli alternatives with fixed density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors, Sobolev slack, \(\operatorname{TV}\le\eta<1-2\alpha\), and \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) ADRF separation. The consumer is the Melaku--Shi (2026) NHANES two-recall diet--mortality mvGPS analysis.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not give a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band under blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets, nor the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band expected-width converse.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning makes the cocycle locally stable, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient whose weights are themselves estimated.
project_justification.fill: The statistical construction uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic-sieve dimensions; finite-sample simultaneous radii for the probability, marked, and multinomial coordinates; a compact joint feasibility set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. Its stability theorem targets \(r_n\) on the joint confidence and regular-count event and controls the complement by bounded clipping. The matching lower frontier remains the explicit fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus, with Low's reduction only a conditional corollary.

body.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery; their qualitative identification theorem requires neither the fixed \(q_e\)-moment radius nor the uniform pair \((\nu_0,c_0)\), which are paper-specific quantitative restrictions here. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands for errors-in-variables regression under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski moment restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not give a sharp shrinking-width result for a marked quotient. Babii gives honest expected-diameter control for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies the testing-to-expected-length reduction used only after the marked modulus is established. These papers inform separate components of the statistical argument; none is presented as a theorem literally tightened by the enabling identification result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The analytic identification of \(q_x\) is expected to be a short corollary once the unmarked law has recovered \(f_x\) and the error laws. The contribution therefore stands or falls on the marked-channel stability and fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus, not on presenting marked identification alone as difficult.
body.honest_scope: The fixed values of \(\beta\), the Sobolev radii, \(p_{\min}\), the paper-specific moment and local spectral constants, and \(\kappa\) are known class indices. The qualitative analytic identification anchor does not need the fixed moment radius or uniform protected-neighborhood constants. Adaptation to smoothness, a local-to-zero spectral-strength phase diagram, growing replicate counts, boundary bands, and computational optimization are outside this specialization. Analytic identification and the unmarked reduction are enabling compatibility results. The explicit simultaneous marked-channel stability theorem remains to be proved, the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the principal open object, and the all-honest-band converse is conditional on resolving that object.
